title: Intel Xe GPU (xpu-exporter)
description: Live view of Intel GPUs from xpu-exporter.

panels.title: GPU $device
panels.description: State: COMPUTING = compute engine running; AWAKE = card awake but not computing (e.g. a model just sitting in VRAM); IDLE = nothing running; SUSPENDED = card asleep, the other tiles are its last readings before sleep; OFFLINE = the exporter is unreachable. Throttle: POWER CAP is the normal ceiling under load, THERMAL needs attention (it has never fired in the retained history). Hottest leaves out the voltage regulator, which while computing (about 5 h of computing in ~9 days of history) ran a median of 77-81 °C and a p90 of 84-90 °C, peaked at 95 °C and has no published limit, so it would often turn this tile yellow during normal inference; it is charted under Details > All sensors. A B70's core reading can hold its last value while the card idles (a known sensor quirk).

targets.expr:
max by (device) (
  label_replace(3 * (xpu_gpu_compute_busy_ratio{device=~"$device"} > bool 0.05) * on(device) (xpu_gpu_idle{device=~"$device"} == bool 0), "k", "c", "", "")
  or label_replace(2 * (xpu_gpu_busy_ratio{device=~"$device"} > bool 0.05) * on(device) (xpu_gpu_idle{device=~"$device"} == bool 0), "k", "b", "", "")
  or label_replace(xpu_gpu_idle{device=~"$device"}, "k", "i", "", "")
) * on(device) group_left(model) xpu_gpu_info

max by (device) (
  label_replace(2 * max by (device) (xpu_gpu_throttled{device=~"$device", reason=~"thermal|prochot|vr_thermalert|vr_tdc|ratl"}), "k", "t", "", "")
  or label_replace(max by (device) (xpu_gpu_throttled{device=~"$device", reason=~"pl1|pl2|pl4"}), "k", "p", "", "")
) * on(device) (xpu_gpu_idle{device=~"$device"} == bool 0)

panels.title: Computing vs awake
panels.description: Solid = compute engine executing (tokens are being generated). Dashed = card awake, which can read 100 % while a model is merely resident (dashed lines are not listed in the legend).

panels.title: VRAM used
panels.description: Bytes resident per card against the card's total (dashed grey). A loaded B70 sits at about 97 to 99 %, which is normal.

panels.title: Core temperature
panels.description: Core die per card. Dashed yellow and red lines are the dashboard's warning marks (85 / 95 °C); hardware critical is 100 °C. A B70 core sensor can freeze at its last value while the card is idle. VR, memory, controller and per-channel VRAM are under Details.

panels.title: Power draw
panels.description: Board power against the enforced cap (dashed grey: 275 W, the B70's rated limit; both B70s share it). Sitting at the cap under load is normal (see POWER CAP in the card above); peaks a little above it are recorded (about 290 W so far). Each point is the peak within its time step, so idle power looks spikier than its average.

panels.title: All sensors -- gpu $device
panels.description: core, memory, vr (voltage regulator: hottest part, no published limit), mctrl, pcie. Critical is 100 °C (memory 105). Each point is the peak within its time step.

panels.title: VRAM channel temperature
panels.description: One row per VRAM channel (16 per B70; the xe driver publishes these). A single hot row is what the aggregate memory sensor averages away.

panels.title: Memory bandwidth
panels.description: Fraction of peak; token generation is bandwidth-bound.

panels.title: Core clock
panels.description: Actual frequency; reads 0 while the card's render engine sleeps in its deepest idle state (C6). Dashed grey = hardware maximum.

panels.title: PCIe throughput
panels.description: rx = card reading host memory (peaks about 15 GB/s during model load, the Gen3 x16 ceiling); tx = card writing host memory.

panels.title: PCIe link
panels.description: Negotiated host link. Both B70s have reported Gen3 (8 GT/s) for the whole retained history (about 9 days), including at full load. They support Gen5 (32 GT/s); if "now" stays below "max", the slot or BIOS is limiting the card (the observed PCIe peak of about 15.5 GB/s equals the Gen3 x16 ceiling).

targets.expr: max by (device, model) (xpu_gpu_pcie_link_width{device=~"$device", kind="current"} * on(device) group_left(model) xpu_gpu_info)
max by (device, model) (xpu_gpu_pcie_link_width{device=~"$device", kind="max"} * on(device) group_left(model) xpu_gpu_info)
max by (device, model) (xpu_gpu_pcie_link_speed_gtps{device=~"$device", kind="current"} * on(device) group_left(model) xpu_gpu_info)
max by (device, model) (xpu_gpu_pcie_link_speed_gtps{device=~"$device", kind="max"} * on(device) group_left(model) xpu_gpu_info)

panels.title: Throttle reasons -- gpu $device
panels.description: pl1, pl2 and pl4 are the sustained, burst and peak power limits and show blue "cap", which is normal under load. thermal, prochot (processor hot), ratl (running-average thermal limit) and vr_thermalert / vr_tdc (voltage regulator) are the ones to act on and show red "THROTTLE". Nothing red has fired in the retained history. Grey = flag reported and clear; blank = no data.

panels.title: Runtime suspend
panels.description: Blue "yes" while the card is runtime-suspended (asleep); every other series holds its last sample while it is set. Grey = awake; blank = no data.
